position.identity: Benson S. Hsu, MD, MBA. Pediatric intensivist and former health system executive. I build with AI, run the data, and decide what's worth it.
position.promise: I help health systems, investors and companies decide which clinical AI to trust, invest in and build on, and how to get it adopted and grow it safely.
position.proof: Every decision is backed by a lab: builds with current models, dated, with the results reported, including what broke, and a verdict on each.
position.method: Four stages: Strategy, Build or buy, Rules, Proof. Every entry and every memo ends in a verdict: Build, Buy, Skip or Wait.

signature_block.name: Benson S. Hsu, MD, MBA
signature_block.line: Pediatric intensivist. Former health system executive.

stages.name: Strategy
stages.question: Should we do this at all, or put money into it, and what will it cost or earn?
stages.background: Health system executive, 2015 to 2019, two of the roles as vice president; the payer side, 2020. Senior Advisor, McKinsey, 2021 to 2023; External Advisor, Bain, 2024: healthcare strategy, organizational change, private equity. Duke MBA. Clients and engagements are confidential. TBD: what may be said publicly about McKinsey and Bain.

stages.name: Build or buy
stages.question: Is what the vendor says true? And is there a part of this we should build ourselves?
stages.background: Five clinical AI tools built with current models and agents, 2026. Enterprise data and analytics for a health system, 2015 to 2017.

stages.name: Rules
stages.question: What will the committee ask for before it signs, and who is watching after go-live?
stages.background: More than fifteen national practice guidelines, the latest the 2026 Surviving Sepsis Campaign children's guideline. Health system AI governance work; TBD: scope wording.

stages.name: Proof
stages.question: Does it work on our patients, and did anyone check again after the model changed?
stages.background: June to July 2026: I checked my own papers against their files. Seven numbers failed; two papers retired. Every verdict here carries its date; a re-run on a newer model gets a new entry rather than a quiet edit.

doors.line: You name the tool. One memo, ten business days, one fixed fee: a recommendation and the list your governance committee will ask for next.
A full read in ten business days, or five to know whether to walk away. Whether the clinical claims hold, and which ones you would have trouble defending in a year.
A physician who has run a health system data shop and built with current models, on your team for the clinical parts. By the day or by the project.

offers.name: Red-flag read
offers.scope: One tool or one company. One page: the deal-breakers, or a statement that there were none, and what the read did not cover
offers.note: If you go on to a tier 2 read of the same target within 90 days, this fee counts toward it.

offers.name: Decision memo or diligence read
offers.scope: The full four-stage memo with a verdict, the cost, and the governance requirements. One revision round.

offers.name: Multi-vendor or portfolio read
offers.scope: Up to three tools or companies, read against one thesis

offers.name: Clinical AI expert on a project
offers.scope: A physician on your team for the clinical parts: what the tool does to a workflow, what the committee will ask, whether the vendor's study holds up
offers.turnaround: By the day or by the project

fee_line: Questions while the work is under way are not billed.
engagement_steps: Half an hour on the phone, no charge, mostly so I can tell you whether I am the right person.
A one-page scope with the fee and the date.
The read itself. A message if a document is missing, otherwise nothing until the memo.
The memo, and one more pass on it if you want changes.

rules.seat: Advisor to a company, or diligence reader on it for a fund, never both. Ask and I will tell you.
will_not: No implementation, no product sales, no expert-network calls.
rules.sells: There is no product here. You get a recommendation in writing and the reasoning behind it.

lines.lab_scope: Everything on the wall so far is pediatric, because that is where I practice. Nothing in the method depends on that.
lines.candidate_not_clinical: The pathways are candidates for a physician to review. None is for clinical use.
lines.verdict_definition: Build, Buy, Skip or Wait is advice to a buyer. It is not a grade on the paper.

how_entries_written: Four sections in one order: worth doing, build or buy, rules, is it working.
The identity line once, at the top of the write-up; the verdict last, with one line of reasoning and one line on what it is worth to a buyer.
Dated. Numbers only from a public deposit or a named source; retired figures never reappear.
Model names reported neutrally. Pathways are candidates, not clinical documents.
Journal status appears only in the status line; numbers may change after review.
disclosure: Tools were built on my own time with no institutional data. Advisory work is disclosed to my employer.
aequitas_separation: Aequitas Health shares no money, staff or data with Celeritas Health.

contact.reply: I reply within two business days.

offers_summary: Three kinds of read, taking 5, 10 or 15 business days, and a day rate for consulting partners. One fee, quoted in writing before I start, and no hours billed against it.
how_i_write: Numbers come from a public deposit or a named source. A retired figure stays retired, even rounded. Each entry names the models and what each did, because by the time you read it they may have changed. Under review means the numbers may move. Pace in 2027: about one entry a quarter, fewer if the clinical work gets busy.
